questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O and P is any point on the circle. If ∠APB = 112°, then what is the measure of ∠OAB ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠APB = 112°

**Concept used:**

Concept of the line segment of the circle

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2833975a477ab8857b4e61d267b4154d6ede3614cd9b7a7a29505a8de3806ac.png] 

In the given figure,

∠APB = 112°

AB is a chord

We know if a chord makes x° on the major arc of the circle then it will make 2x° on the center.

So, ∠AOB = 224°

But angle cannot be greater than 180°

So angle is = 360 - 224

⇒ 136° 

AO = BO = radius of the circle

So,

∠OAB = 44/2 = 22°

**∴ The measure of ∠OAB is 22°**

questions.question: O is the centre of the circle. Its two chord AB and CD intersect each other at the point P (internally) within the circle. If AB = 22 cm, PB = 14 cm, CP = 8 cm, then find the value of the PD.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = 22 cm

PB = 14 cm

CP = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

Power of a Point Theorem: PA × PB = PC × PD

**Calculation:**

Let PA = x cm

Since AB = 22 cm, PA = AB - PB = 22 - 14 = 8 cm

Using the Power of a Point Theorem:

PA × PB = PC × PD

⇒ 8 × 14 = 8 × PD

⇒ 112 = 8 × PD

⇒ PD = 112 / 8

⇒ PD = 14 cm

**The value of PD is 14 cm.**

questions.question: A pair of tangents AB and AC are drawn from a point which is at a distance of 10 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 6 cm, then the area in cm² of quadrilateral ABOC, is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A pair of tangents AB and AC are drawn from a point which is at a distance of 10 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 6 cm.

**Formula used:**

Area of triangle = 1/2 × base × height

Area of quadrilateral = 2 × Area of triangle

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e4eac65a4013956324cc43cd7064a1b4d5ac92352d2a9febb8039a9d5a5619c.png] 

In Δ ABO is congruent to Δ ACO,

Then, Area of quadrilateral ABOC is twice the Area of Δ ABO.

In Δ ABO

OA = 10 cm

OB = 6 cm

Since, tangent is perpendicular to radius at the point of contact.

By pythagoras' theorem,

⇒ AB² = AO² – OB²

⇒ AB = √(AO2 – OB2) 

⇒ √(100 – 36)

⇒ √64

⇒ AB = 8 cm

Area of Δ ABO = (1/2)× AB × OB

⇒ (1/2)× 8 × 6

⇒ 24 cm²

Area of quadrilateral ABOC = 2 × Area of Δ ABO

⇒ 2 × 24 cm²

⇒ 48 cm²

**∴ The area in cm2 of quadrilateral ABOC, is 48.**

questions.question: The distance between two equal parallel chords of a circle is 10 cm. If the chords are 24 cm long, then what is the length of the radius?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equal parallel chords are on opposite sides of the center and equidistant from it.

Distance from center to each chord = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

Half the length of the chord = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

Radius r = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of equal parallel chords AB and CD = 24 cm

Distance between chords (MN) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

A perpendicular drawn from the center to a chord bisects the chord.

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let O be the center of the circle.

⇒ Since the parallel chords are of equal length, they are located on opposite sides and are equidistant from the center.

⇒ Distance from center to chord OM = Total Distance MN ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

⇒ The perpendicular OM bisects the chord AB, so AM = AB ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

⇒ In right-angled ΔOMA, applying Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ r² = 5² + 12²

⇒ r² = 25 + 144 = 169

⇒ r = √169 = 13 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Parallel Chords

If two parallel chords of a circle are equal in length, they must be situated at equal distances from the center and lie on opposite sides of the center.

Perpendicular from Center Rule

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to any chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Pythagorean Triplets

Standard Pythagorean triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) frequently appear in circle geometry to easily relate the radius, chord length, and distance from the center without full calculation.

(Perpendicular)² + (Base)² = (Height)²

In this figure AB = chord OM⊥AB then AM = MB

questions.question: A circle touches the side BC of ΔABC at P and also touches AB and AC produced at Q and R, respectively. If the perimeter of ΔABC = 14.1 cm, then the length (in cm) of AQ will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A circle touches the side BC of ΔABC at P and also touches AB and AC produced at Q and R, respectively.

The perimeter of ΔABC = 14.1 cm

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d640fd4754b17e3fff2873580c35de8c0b065af3e724b8dd682f86c9334b20a7.png] 

AQ = AR [Tangents]

BP = BQ [Tangents]

CP = CR [Tangents]

Perimeter of ΔABC = AB + BP + CP + AC

⇒ 14.1 = AB + BQ + CR + AC

⇒ 14.1 = AQ + AR

⇒ 14.1 = AQ + AQ

⇒ 14.1 = 2AQ

⇒ AQ = (14.1/2) cm

⇒ AQ = 7.05 cm

**∴ The length of AQ is 7.05 cm**

questions.question: Let C be a circle with Centre O and P be an external point to C. Let PQ and PR be the tangents to C such that Q and R be the points of tangency, respectively. If ∠ROQ = 110°, find ∠RPQ.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Centre of the circle, O

External point, P

PQ and PR are tangents to the circle at Q and R respectively

∠ROQ = 110°

**Formula Used:**

∠PQR = 90° and ∠PRQ = 90° (radius of a circle and a tangent line are always perpendicular to each other)

Sum of all angles of Quadrilateral = 360°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2317074d95d312dc9ed6143a828c9218ac2350098401531c70a9971d92aa47a2.png] 

∠ROQ = 110°

Using the formula:

∠ROQ + ∠PQR + ∠PRQ + ∠RPQ = 360°

⇒ 110° + 90° + 90° +∠RPQ = 360°

⇒ ∠RPQ = 360° - 290°

⇒ ∠RPQ = 70°

**The correct answer is option 3:** 70°

questions.question: AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. If C is any point on the circle such that ∠BAC = 42°, then find the measure of ∠BOC.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter = AB 

∠BAC = 42°

**Concept:**

Angle in a semi-circle is a right angle. 

The Sum of all the angles in a triangle is 180°. 

Angles opposite to equal sides are equal in measure. 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0fa78118ce45d1c60b7424c314c7d8746569ccef0bda4c49f39f2422712d257.png] 

In triangle ABC, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180° [Angle sum property]

⇒ 42° + ∠B + 90° = 180° [Angle in a semi-circle is 90°] 

⇒ ∠B = 180° - 90°- 42° = 48° 

In triangle BOC, ∠OBC + ∠BOC + ∠BCO = 180°

⇒ 48° + 48° + ∠BOC = 180° [Angles opposite to equal sides are equal] 

⇒ ∠BOC = 180° - 48° - 48° [ BO = CO = r] 

**∴ ∠BOC = 84° **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** The angle made on the center by a chord is double the angle made on the circumference by the same chord.

∠BOC = 2∠BAC = 2 × 42° 

⇒ 84° 

∴ The required angle is 84°.

questions.question: In a circle with center O, PA and PB are tangent to the circle at A and B, respectively, from an external point P. If, ∠AOB = 116° then what is the measure of ∠OPB?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠AOB = 116° 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af5cc7f5146ebc8f0f370d5c880b76b62e40074e9955c330ce22d8e9b836e205.png] 

According to the question

⇒ ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180° 

⇒ 116° + ∠APB = 180° 

⇒ ∠APB = (180° – 116°)

⇒ ∠APB = 64° 

Now,

⇒ ∠OPB = ∠APB/2

⇒ ∠OPB = 64°/2

⇒ ∠OPB = 32° 

**∴ The required value of ∠OPB is 32°**

questions.question: Chord AB and diameter CD of a circle meet at the point P, outside the circle when it is produced, If PB = 8 cm, AB = 12 cm and distance of P from the centre of the circle is 18 cm, the radius (in cm) of the circle is closest to: [√41 = 6.4]
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

Secant Property

If chord AB and chord CD of a circle intersect at a point P, then

PA × PB = PC × PD

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a5a037a05300d60c7c831cdbc1696d6d5fc671ea6225a2671b97e10f29bf2df.png] 

Let the radius of the circle = r 

PA = 12 + 8 = 20 cm, PB = 8 cm, PC = (18 + r) cm, PD = (18 - r) cm

PA × PB = PC × PD

⇒ 8 × 20 = (18 - r) × (18 + r)

⇒ 160 = 324 - r²

⇒ r² = 164

⇒ r = 12.8062 

**∴ The radius of the circle is closest to 12.8 cm**

questions.question: Let C be a circle with center O and PQ be the diameter of C. Let AB be a chord on C. If ∠QOB = 40°, ∠AOP = 80°, then find ∠AOB.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠QOB = 40º

∠AOP = 80º

**Formula used:**

The sum of all angle on a straight line is 180º.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ee190b6a232f2803868fde3d4a741e2d79399257d32dd04b32f42a70452ccab.png] 

∠QOB = 40º

∠AOP = 80º

Since PQ is the diameter, 

Let ∠AOB = xº

∠AOB + ∠AOP + ∠QOB = 180º (sum of angles on a straight line)

⇒ x + 80º + 40º = 180º

⇒ x + 120º = 180º

⇒ x = 180º - 120º

⇒ x = 60º

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Two circles with centre O and A touch each other externally. The radius of the first circle with centre O is 6 cm. The radius of the second circle with centre A is 3 cm. Find the length of their common tangent CB (in centimetres).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the first circle = 6 cm

Radius of the second circle = 3 cm

**Solution:**

**1. Distance Between the Centers:**

Distance between centers = 6 + 3 = 9 cm

**2. Length of the Common Tangent:**

Length of the common tangent = √[(6 + 3)² - (6 - 3)²]

Substitute the values:

Length of the common tangent = √[9² - 3²]

= √[81 - 9]

= √72

= 6√2

**Answer:**

The length of the common tangent is 6√2 cm.

Formula used:

Circumference(C) of a circle = 2πr

Area of a circle = πr²

Where, r = radius

C = 2 × 22/7 × r

⇒ 132 = 44r/7

r = 21 cm

Now,

Area of a circle = πr2

⇒ 22/7 × 21 × 21 = 1386 cm²

 

∴ The area of circle is 1386 cm2.

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally at any point C. PQ is the direct common tangent to both the circles touching the circles at point P and point Q. If the radii of the circles are 36 cm and 16 cm, respectively, then the length of PQ is:
questions.solution:

Radius of 2nd circle = 16 cm

**Formula used:**

If two circle touches each other externally and a common tangent is passing then,

Length of common tangent = √(4 × r₁ × r₂)

**Calculation:**

Length of common tangent (PQ) = √(4 × 36 × 16)

⇒ 2 × 6 × 4 = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

questions.question:
PBA and PDC are two secants. AD is the diameter of the circle with the centre at O. ∠A = 30°, ∠P = 20°. Find the measure of ∠DBC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/454496cc8df3528f65dea1bbb4d6b3eedb5d3f81f73dfccae801d490f58f71f3.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠A = 30°

∠P = 20°

**Formula used:**

 
• The diameter of a circle subtends an angle of 90° at any point on circle.
 
• Angle subtended from the same arc on the same sides are equal.

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd64111aeca79b31a2e97d4b43b923fe6e23b63b5a5eea39260342a09c93f305.png] **

Since,The diameter of a circle subtends an angle of 90° at any point on circle

So, ∠ABD = 90°

and, Angle subtended from the same arc on the same sides are equal.

So, ∠DAB = ∠DCB = 30°

Now,

∠ADC = 30 + 20 = 50 (external angle of Δ ADP)

In ΔCDQ

∠ CQD = 180 - (30 + 50) = 180 - 80 = 100° 

Now,

∠ CQD = ∠ AQB = 100° -- (alternate angle)

So,

∠ABQ = 180 - (100 + 30) = 180 - 130 = 50° 

Thus, ∠DBC = 90 - ∠ABQ = 90 - 50 = 40° 

**∴ The measure of ∠DBC is 40°.**

questions.question: If the diameter of a circle bisects each of the two chords of the circle, then both of the chords:

The relation between the two chords

If the radius bisects the chord, then the radius is perpendicular to the chord

AB and CD are two chords

PQ is a diameter with a center O

⇒ ∠CFO = 90° 

⇒ ∠AEO + ∠CFO = 90° + 90° 

⇒ ∠AEO + ∠CFO = 180°

questions.question: Two circles of radii 9 cm and 4 cm, respectively, touch each other externally at point A. PQ is the direct common tangent of those two circles of centres O₁ and O₂, respectively. The length of PQ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

The radii of both circles are 9 cm and 4 cm

Both circles touch each other at point A externally

PQ is the common tangent of both circles.

Calculations:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3bac1d32bfade07ef074bcc877b6c79563f80bd2823caba6b424da1595303fb1.png] 

Length of a direct common tangent, when 2 circles are touching externally, 

⇒ √[d² - (R - r)²]

where D is the distance between 2 centres

R and r are 2 radii of circles

Calculation:

Using the formula, we get

⇒ √[132 - (9 - 4)²]

⇒ √144 = 12

∴ The length of PQ = 12 cm.
